speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is why Singapore is a strong advocate for a multilateral, rules-based approach to addressing climate change.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We work with other like-minded countries at the United Nations (UN) to push for the best possible multilateral deal on climate change.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are privileged to have played an instrumental facilitator role in these talks, which culminated with the adoption of the Paris Agreement in 2015 and the agreements on the Katowice Climate Package in 2018 as well as the Chile Madrid Time for Action in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While not perfect, these agreements will help to establish a virtuous cycle of climate actions by all countries.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The challenge is to maintain this momentum of global climate action at a time when the multilateral system is under strain.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Singapore will continue our active and constructive engagement in the negotiations.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will work with other countries, including the incoming United Kingdom (UK) Conference of the Parties (COP)-26 Presidency, to strengthen the multilateral framework of cooperation on climate change and push for a good outcome at the next Climate Conference in Glasgow.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Regionally, we have taken an active role to galvanise climate action.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As Chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in 2018, we convened the first-ever Special ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Climate Action (SAMCA) and Expanded-SAMCA, where ASEAN and China, Japan and the Republic of Korea (ROK) reaffirmed our political commitments and discussed ways to step up regional climate action.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have collaborated with partners to improve our understanding of climate change and its impact, through research and institutions like the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre, which is based in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through our Climate Action Package, we have partnered and supported fellow developing countries to implement their Paris commitments and enhance climate action.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In October 2019, we co-organised with New Zealand a workshop on the Paris rulebook to help countries in the region better understand their obligations under the Paris Agreement and to identify concrete actions and strategies that can be pursued.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Just last month, we co-organised with the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) Partnership and the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Secretariat another workshop to discuss how ASEAN countries can update their climate pledges.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We hope that this workshop will facilitate the submission of updated climate pledges from ASEAN countries this year.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Looking ahead, we will work with Vietnam, as ASEAN Chair this year, to sustain the momentum of climate action in the region.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are also taking strong action at home.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Notwithstanding our constraints in deploying renewable energy at scale, we are committed to playing our full part to tackle climate change and transform our economy towards a low-carbon future.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The revenue will be used to support emission reduction projects and help businesses become more resource- and energy-efficient.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our Zero Waste Masterplan will transform Singapore into a Circular Economy, where materials are retained and reused in the value chain for as long as possible.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will help to reduce our carbon footprint and complement our efforts to address climate change.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government can only do so much on our own.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are, therefore, heartened that Singaporeans, especially our youths, understand the importance of this issue and are prepared to take climate-friendly actions in a whole-of-nation effort to address climate change.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In 2018, we had a successful Year of Climate Action rallying community groups, grassroots organisations, corporations, schools and non-governmental organisations to take action for a sustainable future.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Collectively, we held more than 800 climate action-related events across the People, Private, Public (3P) sectors, equivalent to two events a day.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More than 342,000 individuals, organisations and educational institutions have pledged to take climate action.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In 2019, we sustained the momentum with an inaugural Climate Action Week which featured ground-up activities organised by our 3P partners.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This year, we continue to encourage Singaporeans to work with us to co-create and co-deliver solutions to game-change climate change.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Climate change is an existential challenge for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To ensure that future generations can continue to enjoy a vibrant and liveable city, we will continue to put sustainability at the centre of everything we do and work with 3P partners and Singaporeans to combat climate change and transition towards a climate resilient and low-carbon future.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We recognise that by our actions alone we cannot stop climate change.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But we hope that through our actions, we can play our small part to catalyse change and contribute to international and regional efforts to galvanise climate action.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am very encouraged by the very proactive affirmations that the Minister has made.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Notwithstanding what we do to tackle this global issue, we will inevitably be affected by what others in the region do or not do.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My question to the Minister is: is there anything that we can do to encourage and get, in particular, the neighbouring countries to also do their part so that, as a whole, no one needs to suffer the consequences of another country's inaction in this regard?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Actually, until 2015, the whole world was waiting for everybody to do something, but not themselves.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is what we call the "Nationally Determined Commitments".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While the first stage was to get everybody to do their best and to follow the rules in committing to deliver their best, in reality, Science is telling us, you have to do much more than what you are doing today.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That will put us on a better footing, once we get the 2015 Paris Agreement actually operational.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is already a big problem facing many countries as we see, as we go year after year, trying to get the rules agreed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But I am quite optimistic that at the end of the day, leaders, politicians are listening.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Leaders and politicians all over the world are listening to their youths, loud and clear.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They want to make sure that their future is a sustainable future and, even in Singapore, we really have to resteer our economy, the way we live, to make sure that what we do now will also deliver a sustainable future for our children and generations to come.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think the Minister shared the good news that Singapore will be updating our climate pledge.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just check when will we be doing so?
